title: Security Zones and Policies: The Complete Beginner's Guide

scenes.narration: A Junos firewall divides your network into zones. Think of them as floors in an office building. And a security guard between each floor.

scenes.heading: The security desk
scenes.narration: The lobby is public, the second floor is sales, and the server room is high security. The guard controls who moves between them. Each floor is a zone. Moving within a floor is allowed. Moving between floors needs a policy.

scenes.heading: A policy
scenes.narration: A policy names a source zone, a destination zone, and the action. The first matching policy wins. And if nothing matches, the traffic is denied. A policy names the two zones. Then what it matches. And the action to take.

scenes.heading: Common mix-ups
scenes.narration: Three misunderstandings. Traffic inside a zone is allowed by default. Policies reference zones, not interfaces. And if nothing matches, the traffic is denied.

scenes.heading: Remember this
scenes.cta: Try the Courseiva Junos security lab
scenes.narration: So, to recap. Interfaces belong to zones, and one interface lives in one zone. Between zones is denied by default, and inside a zone is allowed. Policies are checked top down, first match wins. Ready to practise? Try the Courseiva Junos security lab.
